To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

HU induces an up-regulation of genes involved in the transport of small molecules and anions into the cells and a down-regulation of those genes involved in the cell junction, adhesion and extracellular matrix.

HU induces a significant redistribution of fluids from caudal to cephalad body parts and an alteration of the normal head-to-foot blood pressure gradient, with consequent changes in brain gene expression.
microgravity and fluid redistribution induced by hindlimb unloading cause a redistribution of fluids and ions from the caudad (tail) to the cephalic (head) portion of the body.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a global analysis of gene profile changes associated to microgravity and fluid-shift in the mouse brain.
the study of the effects of microgravity and fluid redistribution on the brain, with particular attention to the molecular mechanisms underlying the changes in the gene expression profile.
the identification of molecular mechanisms involved in the brain response to microgravity and fluid redistribution.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the HU treatment, by inducing a shift of fluids from the lower part of the body to the brain, induces a significant transcriptomic reprogramming in the brain of mice, affecting a wide range of cellular pathways and functions.
the transcriptomic changes in the mouse brain following HU treatment reflect the effects of a redistribution of fluids and a loss of hydrostatic pressure gradients.
HU induces a redistribution of fluids in the brain with a consequent alteration of the normal ionic and molecular gradients.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
HU induces a redistribution of fluids and ions in the body and brain, which leads to changes in ion channel and transporter expression, and to an alteration in the balance of the coagulation system.

microgravity and HU cause changes in gene expression in the brain, which are likely to be involved in altered fluid and ion distribution, blood coagulation, immune response, learning, and memory processes.
microgravity causes a shift toward a state that resembles the one of a hyper-coagulative condition and a decrease in learning and memory processes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
HU induces an alteration in the expression of genes involved in the regulation of ion channels, blood clotting, synaptic plasticity and cell junction.
the brain is highly sensitive to microgravity and fluid redistribution and that these changes are reflected by the expression of genes involved in a variety of cellular processes.
the HU mouse is a good model for studying the effects of microgravity and fluid redistribution on the central nervous system.
